chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad al-Qindy, who said:

I entered Medina and with me was my brother Sayf, and the people had been struck with nosebleed, so that if a man had a nosebleed for two days, he died. So I returned to the house and found Sayf with a severe nosebleed. So I entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said: 'O Ziyad! Feed Sayf the apple.' So I fed it to him, and he was cured.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the apple in curing nosebleeds according to Imam al-Hadi (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the medical wisdom of Imam al-Hadi (AS) during a specific epidemic of severe epistaxis in Medina, demonstrating the intersection of spiritual authority and practical healing. The specific prescription of apples (*tuffah*) underscores the Shia tradition of recognizing therapeutic properties in natural foods, a concept often linked to the broader Islamic emphasis on *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine). It serves as a scholarly reference for the efficacy of dietary interventions in treating acute physical ailments within the Imami tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad Al Qindy who said,

‘I entered Al-Medina and with me was my brother Sayf and the people had been struck with nose-bleed, and it was so that when the man had nose-bleed for two days, he died. So I returned to the house and Sayf had nose-bleed with intense bleeding. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ziyad! Feed Sayf the apple’. So I fed it to him, so he was cured’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Ziyad al-Qandiy who has said the following: “

I once entered al-Madinah with my brother Sayf. People suffered from nasal hemorrhage because of which a man after two days died. I returned to my lodging and found Sayf with nasal hemorrhage severely. I went to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘O Ziyad feed Sayf apples.’ I fed him apples and he got well.’”
